messages.subject: CSV Output - ERROR
messages.body_plain:
Help! — I am using the "epochvalues2csv = TRUE” setting to pull out the individual epoch values (ENMO) for each time point, because I want to calculate ENMO (and other things) for some very specific intervals each day.

I’ve noticed a bug in GGIR. The CSV output (found in the output/meta/csv folder) looks correct for the first couple days of my recording. But, after the third day, although the timestamp keeps increasing correctly, the values (both ENMO and anglez) keep repeating over the 24-hour period the same values from day 3.

See the attached CSV output as an example. Look at June 7, 8, 9, 10 — the output is exactly the same for each of these days!

Hopefully it’s an easy fix??

Thanks,

Graydon

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] CSV Output - ERROR
messages.body_plain:
I think I found the problem, and the solution. Although I was using “strategy = 1” for Part 2, it looks like the epochvalues2csv is sensitive to what you put as the ndayswindow. If you put a value in dayswindow less than the actual number of days in your data, regardless of the “strategy” the epoch2values setting does not export the epoch values beyond ndayswindow and just repeats the epochs for the last full “ndayswindow” until a time point that would be the end of the data file.

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Results Interpretation
messages.body_plain:
These are averages across days, so no need to divide by number of days.
If you want day specific estimates then use the day specific csv report.
Note that these estimates are the total time spent per class, with no consideration of 'bouts'. For time spent in bouted behaviour see documentation.
Vincent

I have looked into the files you sent me and discovered the problem.
Due to changes earlier this year GGIR is not able anymore to process more than one non-angle metric.
I have now fixed that in the GitHub branch "issue247_1to6bug" in case you are familiar with GitHub.
If not, then do not worry, this will be included in the next release of GGIR. After that you will be able to work with multiple non-angle metrics again.

In the meantime, you should be able to process your files by turning off the addition metrics, e.g. do.en = FALSE.
Best, Vincent

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] MVPA threshold for adults
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I find it surprising that you had participants who thought they were not very active, but had over 200 minutes of MVPA per day. From my experience, it is quite common to get 0 minutes MVPA per day (at Hildebrand threshold) with participants who are not active.  Are you sure that your raw acceleration data is being saved in g-units? This large amount of MVPA might be happening if your raw data is  in m/s/s, so would probably be worth investigating that as a first step.

Matt

messages.body_plain:
Hi Giulia,
Those recordings are probably too short for meaningful analysis with GGIR, you would have to change argument windowsizes to be able to process such a short file.
My advise is to look out for a multi-day recording. I think shared one in this google group before.

Other tips:
- If you have GENEActiv data focus on the bin file format it produces. GGIR is best test for these.
- check that you do not have any non-acceleromater csv files in the folder specified by datadir, GGIR is may be confused if it encounters other csv files that are not accelerometer data.
- set print.filename = TRUE and do.parallel=FALSE, in that way you can check that GGIR is trying to process the actual file you are interested in.
Vincent
